name: Fat grafting (lower eyelid / tear trough)

lead: Fat grafting takes a small amount of your own fat from another body area and places it in the hollow between the lower lid and cheek, softening the tear trough and giving a smoother transition. Forum users discuss it as a longer-lasting alternative to hyaluronic acid filler.

The harvested fat is processed and injected as volume under the thin eyelid skin, filling the depression. Proponents also say the transferred tissue may improve skin quality, which researchers are still studying. A systematic review found the literature was mostly case reports and retrospective case series.

paras: It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon, sometimes combined with lower blepharoplasty. Fat is collected, prepared and placed in the eye area, with results settling as swelling goes down.

Reported problems with fat grafting include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpy or uneven contours, partial reabsorption of the fat and fat necrosis. The thin eyelid skin makes irregularities more visible, and results can shift with major weight change.

chain: Own fat moved into tear trough
angle.text: Fat from elsewhere on your body is placed in the under-eye hollow, so the tear trough softens and the lid-to-cheek transition looks smoother. Evidence comes mostly from case series.

lead: Fat grafting of the lower eyelid and tear trough, also called periorbital lipofilling or autologous fat transfer, is a surgical procedure in which a patient's own fat is harvested from another part of the body, processed and injected into the hollow beneath the lower eyelid to restore volume and smooth the transition to the cheek [1].

It is used for people who are bothered by a pronounced tear trough, hollow under-eye contour or volume loss, and is sometimes combined with lower blepharoplasty [1][2]. In looksmaxxing communities it appears in discussions of hardmaxxing options for the eye area, alongside fillers and eyelid surgery.

A systematic review of eyelid fat grafting noted that the published literature consisted mostly of case reports and retrospective case series, with no earlier study assessing overall complication or satisfaction rates across techniques [3]. The evidence base is therefore described as limited.
infobox: Lower eyelid, tear trough, sometimes upper eyelid
Surgical technique performed by licensed surgeons

paras: Fat transfer is done in stages: fat is harvested, processed, and injected in small amounts into the target area [1]. Around the eyes it is used to improve lower-eyelid contour and make up for volume loss [1].

Facial rejuvenation has shifted in recent decades from removing tissue toward restoring volume, often combined with repositioning of tissue [1]. Fat grafting and transconjunctival fat repositioning are both used for the tear trough, and the two can be combined in a single operation [2].

A systematic review published in 2016 examined indications, technique and complications of eyelid fat grafting and found that the literature was made up mostly of case reports and retrospective case series [3]. The authors set out to determine outcomes, complications and patient satisfaction across the techniques used [3].

A registered retrospective follow-up study (n=120) looked at lower-eyelid melanin and wrinkles after blepharoplasty for lower-eyelid bags, which is related but concerns blepharoplasty rather than fat grafting itself [4]. A registered phase 1/2 trial of autologous stromal vascular fraction, a fat-derived cell preparation, for skin regeneration has also been listed [5]. No randomized trial comparing fat grafting with hyaluronic acid filler in the tear trough appears in the sources reviewed.

Complications listed for fat transfer in general include swelling, bruising, hematoma, infection, hypertrophic scarring at the donor site, contour irregularities and injury to underlying structures from the cannula [1]. The body may reabsorb a portion of grafted fat, and fat necrosis is a recognized risk [1]. Large weight gain or loss can alter the result because transferred fat behaves like fat elsewhere in the body [1].
The systematic review of eyelid fat grafting specifically addressed complication rates, reflecting that the thin periorbital tissue is a sensitive site [3].

Users on looksmax.org post before-and-after results of eyelid fat grafting. In one thread about an upper-eyelid result, the poster described a very positive experience, while a reply said fat grafting can address visible hollowing but that an underlying ptosis problem is often also present, so it may treat symptoms rather than causes. Another reply described searching for a surgeon abroad who publishes real before-and-after photos.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, eyelid fat grafting is discussed as a surgical route to fuller upper and lower eyelids, with surgeon selection and visible before-and-after results a recurring concern.

claims.claim: Fat grafting can fix hollow eyelids and make the eye area look better.
Fat grafting may only treat symptoms if there is an underlying ptosis problem.
